title: Struct Methods
story: Your profile app needs each person to introduce themselves. Instead of writing a separate function for each person, you want the Person itself to know how to say hello!
why: Methods attach behavior directly to a struct, so every instance can perform actions on its own data.
analogy: A method is like a skill attached to a character in a game — a Warrior can 'attack', a Healer can 'heal'. The skill belongs to the character type.
try_it: Add a `greet_friend` method that takes another Person's name as a parameter and prints "Hi [friend], I'm [name]!"
tips: The first parameter of every method is `self` — it represents the instance the method is called on
Inside a method, you can access fields directly by name — no `self.name` needed, just `name`
common_mistakes: Forgetting `self` as the first parameter — every method needs it
Trying to call a method like a function: `introduce(alice)` is wrong, use `alice.introduce()`
Using `self.name` inside the method body — fields are implicit, just write `name`
